import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import least_squares
eps=df['eps'].values; T=df['T'].values; s=df['sigma'].values
def mk(g):
    def f(pp):
        c,q=pp[0],pp[1]
        X=np.column_stack([1/eps, eps/(1+c*eps)*T**3, T*np.log(T), g(q)/eps])
        b=np.linalg.lstsq(X,s,rcond=None)[0]
        return np.nan_to_num(s-X@b,nan=1e3)
    best=None
    for c0 in [0.5,0.62,0.8]:
        for q0 in [0.3,0.45,0.6]:
            try:
                sol=least_squares(f,[c0,q0],xtol=1e-15,ftol=1e-15,gtol=1e-15,max_nfev=1000)
                if best is None or sol.cost<best.cost: best=sol
            except Exception: pass
    X=np.column_stack([1/eps, eps/(1+best.x[0]*eps)*T**3, T*np.log(T), g(best.x[1])/eps])
    b=np.linalg.lstsq(X,s,rcond=None)[0]
    return np.mean(best.fun**2)/np.var(s), best.x, b
print("p=1/3 exp(-qT):", mk(lambda q: T**(1/3)*np.exp(-q*T)))
print("p=1/3 exp(-q T):", mk(lambda q: np.cbrt(T)*np.exp(-q*T)))
